newsitem.title: GERMANY: Continental talking to Boeing, Airbus about jets.
newsitem.headline: Continental talking to Boeing, Airbus about jets.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc. is talking to both Boeing Co. and Airbus Industrie about buying up to 40 long-range passenger jets, Chairman Gordon Bethune said Wednesday.
Bethune said during a break in an economic conference here he would make a decision "within two months" on whether to buy Boeing 767-400s or 777s or Airbus A320-200s.
Bethune, who heads fifth-largest U.S. passenger carrier, said most of the new aircraft would replace McDonnell-Douglas Corp. DC-10s, which Continental wants to retire from its fleet.
Additional aircraft also would be needed to service routes from the United States to Moscow, and Sao Paolo and Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, which Continental has recently added to its itinerary.
Bethune, a former Boeing executive, said he had no preference at the moment over who should supply the 30 to 40 aircraft he wanted to buy.
He said the newly developed A330 had "a good fit for the size of the aircraft. Whether it offers the best long-term investment, we'll have to decide."
"Ultimately, we're going to need 30 to 40 airplanes and we're going to have to decide where to get them," he said.
Part of the planned purchase would be in the form of options, Bethune said.
He put a rough price tag on each plane of $60 million to $70 million, putting the total order price into a range of $1.8 to $2.8 billion.
Bethune dismissed plans by the Airbus consortium to develop a high-capacity super-jumbo -- codenamed A3XX -- saying that it would be hard to operate such a plane profitably.

There would be simply too many low-fare economy class passengers for high-paying executive travellers to subsidise. He added that business travellers wanted high-speed, direct travel to their destinations.
"Non-stop -- that's what people want," he said.
The Airbus consortium groups France's Aerospatiale, British Aerospace, Daimler-Benz Aerospace of Germany and Spain's CASA.
